Reviewed `soph/batched-cutover-drops-resume-marker` (PR 117) — 6 files, +1337/-10 — against `main`. Build, vet, and the full `gitproto`/`strategy`/`syncer` suites pass, including the new tests under `-race`; no live data race exists on `Pusher.lastRejections`, `syncSession.rejections`, or the new test fixtures (every push, `OnRejection` callback, `refRefused` read, and marker decision runs on the single goroutine driving `Execute`; `progressReporter.notify` is mutex-guarded and `terminate()` joins the ticker before the test reads its buffer). The real defects are in ordering/TOCTOU and in the new "silence = refusal" rule, not in memory safety.

```json
[
  {
    "file": "internal/gitproto/push.go",
    "line": 510,
    "summary": "The new \"a command the target never mentioned is a rejection\" loop fires onRejection with a client-invented status, which contradicts the sibling rule in bootstrap.go that silence must never stop a run — and it has zero test coverage.",
    "failure_scenario": "Target advertises report-status but its report omits a status line for one command (a no-op Old==New update, a normalizing/non-conformant server or proxy). sendReceivePack synthesizes onRejection(cmd.Name, \"target reported no status for this ref\"). If that command is the bootstrap temp ref, executeBatched:730 aborts the whole multi-GB import with \"target refused refs/gitsync/bootstrap/heads/X: target reported no status for this ref\" — even though nothing was refused, and two lines above the code states \"treating that silence as a refusal would fail every batched bootstrap\". In any --all-refs (BestEffort) sync it also lands in s.rejections, so applyRejections downgrades a ref that actually landed to ActionWarn with Reason \"target rejected ref update: target reported no status for this ref\" (a client inference attributed to the target) and Pushed/Warned are misreported. `grep -rn \"target reported no status\" internal/` matches only push.go:517 — no test exercises the branch."
  },
  {
    "file": "internal/strategy/bootstrap/bootstrap.go",
    "line": 901,
    "summary": "resolvePendingMarkers deletes the resume marker whenever the branch name exists on the target at ANY hash, discarding the resume position precisely in the case where this run's import did not land.",
    "failure_scenario": "BestEffort batched bootstrap of a large repo. The target refuses `refs/heads/main` with \"already exists\" because a concurrent sync created it at an older commit C; our marker refs/gitsync/bootstrap/heads/main holds our fully-pushed tip T. `refsNow[main]` = C, non-zero, so `IsZero()` is false and the marker is deleted. Commits C..T become unreferenced on the target and the next run re-transfers them — the exact full-re-transfer cost the PR exists to prevent. The test TestExecuteBatchedRefusedButPresentBranchDeletesMarker deliberately seeds an unrelated hash (6dcf09a3…, not h.trunkTip), so this is asserted rather than accidental. The check should be `!refsNow[marker.branch].Equal(<hash we tried to create>)` → keep."
  },
  {
    "file": "internal/strategy/bootstrap/bootstrap.go",
    "line": 921,
    "summary": "The deferred marker-cleanup push is the only push in the new code that does not consult refRefused, so a refused or unacked marker delete is completely silent — the opposite of the identical situation 100 lines above.",
    "failure_scenario": "Under BestEffort, PushCommands returns nil when the target ng's a per-ref delete (deletes blocked in refs/gitsync/*, or Old no longer matches). resolvePendingMarkers logs and notices nothing, so the run reports success while the marker survives on a route the PR itself says has no prune to reap it. The confirmed path at bootstrap.go:815-825 does check and emits \"remove it by hand or let a --prune run reap it\"; this path does not. Additionally, all deletes ride one PushCommands call, so if the marker count exceeds MaxRefUpdates and chunk 1 fails, chunks 2..n are never attempted and the single aggregate notice claims \"could not delete %d\" for all of them."
  },
  {
    "file": "internal/syncer/syncer.go",
    "line": 626,
    "summary": "targetRefsNow uses the receive-pack advertisement as the authority on \"is the branch there\", but receive.hideRefs makes that advertisement an unreliable authority — the exact hazard Config.TargetAssertedEmpty documents in this same file.",
    "failure_scenario": "Target sets receive.hideRefs covering the created branch (Config's own doc, verified against git 2.53: \"receive.hideRefs omits matching refs from receive-pack's advertisement, so a populated target can advertise nothing but the capabilities^{} sentinel and read as empty\"). The branch is created successfully, the listing reports it absent, and the marker is kept forever on the Bootstrap() route that forbids --prune. If hideRefs hides everything, decodeV1AdvRefs returns transport.ErrEmptyRemoteRepository, so the operator gets the misleading notice \"could not confirm refs/heads/main on the target (list target refs: remote repository is empty)\" on a target that plainly holds the branch."
  },
  {
    "file": "internal/strategy/bootstrap/bootstrap.go",
    "line": 233,
    "summary": "The fix is applied only to the batched path; the one-shot resume path still strands its marker permanently on the Bootstrap() route, for exactly the reason executeBatched cites as why it could not defer to prune.",
    "failure_scenario": "`gitsync bootstrap` (Bootstrap(), which rejects --prune at syncer.go:1338) resumes from a marker but the repo is small enough that TargetMaxPack never engages, so Execute takes the one-shot branch. Its comment says the marker is deliberately not deleted and \"Prune is the cleaner instead\" — but on this route no prune run can ever exist, which is the exact argument bootstrap.go:786-789 makes for adding the conditional delete to the batched path. Result: a refs/gitsync/bootstrap/heads/<branch> marker that no code path ever removes. Params.TargetRefsNow is now available here and unused; the one-shot path could settle it the same way."
  },
  {
    "file": "internal/strategy/bootstrap/bootstrap.go",
    "line": 863,
    "summary": "Moving marker cleanup from immediately-after-cutover to after every branch and the tail phase opens a long concurrent-run window between the ref listing and the delete.",
    "failure_scenario": "Branch A's create is unconfirmed at minute 5; the tail phase then fetches and pushes tags for another 20 minutes. During that window a second git-sync run discovers the marker, routes via ReasonBootstrapResumeMarker, and starts resuming from it. Our resolvePendingMarkers then lists (branch now present, created by that run), and deletes the marker at Old=marker.resumeHash — pulling the resume anchor out from under the concurrent run, whose next CAS push against that hash fails. Conversely, if the concurrent run advanced the marker first, our CAS delete silently no-ops (see the refRefused gap above) and we report a cleanup that never happened. The whole listing is also read once for all markers, so any marker whose branch is deleted between the listing and the batched delete push is reaped anyway."
  },
  {
    "file": "internal/strategy/bootstrap/bootstrap.go",
    "line": 791,
    "summary": "createConfirmed is documented as answering for \"the push that just returned\", but there is a reachable cutover path where no push happened in this iteration at all, so it reads the previous branch's LastRejections.",
    "failure_scenario": "adjustedBootstrapTargetRefs (line 328) zeroes the branch when both the branch AND its temp ref already sit at SourceHash, so a create plan is built for an already-complete branch. In executeBatched, BootstrapResumeIndex returns len(Checkpoints) so the checkpoint loop pushes nothing, and the guard at line 767 is false because p.TargetRefs[branch] is non-zero — so the resume cutover push is skipped too. createConfirmed(branch) then indexes a map left over from the previous batch iteration's temp-ref delete (or, for the first batch, a nil map from a Pusher that has never pushed). The outcome happens to be benign in today's reachable states, but the invariant Params.RefRefused and syncSession.refRefused both state (\"read after a push returns\") is violated, and nothing in the code enforces it."
  },
  {
    "file": "internal/gitproto/push.go",
    "line": 70,
    "summary": "LastRejections hands out the Pusher's live internal map and cannot distinguish \"clean push\" from \"no push yet\" or \"no report decoded\" — the ambiguity the caller then has to patch with a separate hand-threaded flag.",
    "failure_scenario": "A caller that mutates the returned map (or ranges it while a multi-request logical push — PushObjects/PushPack split by chunkRefUpdates call sendReceivePack several times per call — is still adding entries) corrupts or mis-reads Pusher state; the doc only forbids retaining it, not mutating it. Because an empty map means three different things, the syncer has to pass gitproto.TargetFeatures.ReportStatus across two package boundaries as Params.TargetReportsRefStatus, whose own doc admits \"leaving it false there costs a ref listing\". A `func (p *Pusher) RefLanded(name) (bool, string)` on the Pusher — which already holds p.Adv and can answer capability.ReportStatus itself — would make the contract enforceable and delete the flag."
  },
  {
    "file": "internal/strategy/bootstrap/bootstrap.go",
    "line": 839,
    "summary": "The tail phase re-derives its fetch haves from `batches` instead of the completedRefs map the new code carefully maintains, re-adding exactly the refs the PR just decided not to claim.",
    "failure_scenario": "`tailTargetRefs[batch.Plan.TargetRef] = batch.Plan.SourceHash` runs unconditionally over every batch, so it claims as a have (a) a subsumed branch whose create was just refused and deliberately withheld from completedRefs at line 421-427, and (b) a branch whose create is sitting in `pending` and deliberately absent from completedRefs at line 791-806 — while omitting the temp refs at `current` that are the things actually holding those objects on the target. Today the objects happen to be present anyway (pinned by the temp ref or the trunk), so no pack breaks; the cost is that the one map the PR maintains as ground truth is bypassed by the very next block, so any future change to what counts as \"delivered\" silently fails to reach the tail fetch. Use completedRefs."
  },
  {
    "file": "internal/strategy/bootstrap/bootstrap.go",
    "line": 929,
    "summary": "The package-level targetRefsNow wrapper adds nothing over the field it calls, and its name collides with both Params.TargetRefsNow and syncSession.targetRefsNow.",
    "failure_scenario": "`refs, err := p.TargetRefsNow(ctx); if err != nil { return nil, err }; return refs, nil` is exactly `return p.TargetRefsNow(ctx)`, so the function reduces to a nil check that could be inlined into resolvePendingMarkers. Three same-named entities (bootstrap.targetRefsNow, Params.TargetRefsNow, syncSession.targetRefsNow) across two packages makes a grep for the ref-listing call site ambiguous and invites editing the wrong one."
  },
  {
    "file": "internal/syncer/syncer.go",
    "line": 623,
    "summary": "targetRefsNow guards s.target.conn but not s.target itself, and it silently drops the skipped-ref-name count that newSession tracks and warns about for the same listing.",
    "failure_scenario": "`if s.target.conn == nil` nil-derefs when s.target is nil (the needTarget=false sessions built by Probe/Fetch); the method is only reachable via bootstrap today, so it is latent rather than live. Separately, `refs, _, err := gitproto.AdvRefsToSlice(adv)` discards the skipped names that newSession:902-910 both warns about and stores as s.target.skippedRefCount — so the map the marker decision is made on can disagree with the session's own view of the target, and a name dropped as invalid reads as \"branch absent\" with no second warning to the operator (safe direction, but the divergence is invisible). The three-line listing block is also a verbatim duplicate of newSession:900-911 and could be one shared helper."
  },
  {
    "file": "internal/syncer/integration_test.go",
    "line": 3219,
    "summary": "The PR documents the doubled-ng-prefix hazard and fixes its own new fixture, but leaves the pre-existing sibling fixture emitting the malformed status it warns about.",
    "failure_scenario": "refCreateDenier.hook's new comment says \"go-git encodes 'ng <ref> <Status>', so a status carrying its own 'ng ' prefix reaches the operator doubled\", and the new test asserts `!strings.Contains(plan.Reason, \"ng deny\")`. Meanwhile integration_test.go:1259 and :3219 still set `Status: \"ng simulated checkpoint pack failure\"`, so CommandStatus.encode writes `ng <ref> ng simulated checkpoint pack failure` and those tests assert against a wire shape no real receive-pack produces. Any assertion built on that Reason string is calibrated to the wrong text."
  }
]

Address race-focused review: answer per ref, compare hashes, narrow the window

The reviewer found no live data race — every push, callback, and marker
decision runs on the goroutine driving Execute, and the fixture state guarded
last round holds under -race. What it found instead were ordering faults and
one rule I got backwards.

**"Silence is a refusal" was wrong, and it was mine.** Last round's gitproto
change synthesized a rejection for a command the target's report never
mentioned. That contradicted the guard two lines above it, which says treating
silence as a refusal would fail every batched bootstrap against a
non-reporting target: an omitted status for a temp ref would have aborted a
multi-gigabyte import over something nothing refused, and it attributed a
client inference to the target in the operator-visible reason. It also had no
test.

Silence is a third answer. Pusher.LastOutcome now reports applied, refused, or
unknown per ref, computed from what the target actually said, and the strategy
treats unknown as doubt — settled against the target's ref listing, never as a
refusal and never as success. This also deletes Params.TargetReportsRefStatus:
the Pusher holds the advertisement, so the capability question belongs to it
rather than being hand-threaded across two packages. LastOutcome answers by
value, so no caller can mutate or race with push state it does not own.

**The cleanup deleted the marker whenever the branch name existed, at any
hash.** A concurrent sync that created the branch at an older commit C left our
marker holding the only reference to C..tip; the marker was deleted anyway and
those commits became unreferenced — the full re-transfer this PR exists to
prevent, in the one case where the import genuinely had not landed. Cleanup now
requires the branch to be at the hash this run pushed; anything else keeps the
marker and says which hash it found. The test that asserted the old behaviour
seeded an unrelated hash, so it was asserting the bug: it now covers both
sides.

**Ordering, all from the review:**

- The settlement ran after the tail phase, leaving the ref listing minutes stale
  while tags pushed — long enough for a concurrent run to adopt the marker and
  start resuming from it before we deleted it. It now runs as soon as the last
  create has happened.
- The deferred delete was the only push in the new code not checked for
  refusal, so a refused cleanup was silent — the opposite of the identical case
  100 lines above. Checked per marker now.
- createConfirmed could read the previous branch's answer on the one path where
  a create plan exists but no push carries it (branch and marker both already at
  the source hash). The code now tracks whether the create was pushed and treats
  that path as what it is: a branch the target already holds, marker stale.
- The tail phase re-derived its fetch haves from the plans, re-claiming exactly
  the creates the cutover withheld. It uses completedRefs, the map the run
  maintains as ground truth.

Smaller: targetRefsNow guards a nil target session (latent via Probe/Fetch) and
documents that receive.hideRefs can hide a ref that is there — safe in this
direction, since a hidden branch reads as absent and keeps a marker that was
not needed; the redundant package-level listing wrapper is gone; and three
pre-existing fixtures still emitted "ng "-prefixed statuses that go-git encodes
a second time, which this PR's own comment warns about.

Still open, and still the user's call: the one-shot path defers marker cleanup
to a prune that Bootstrap() forbids — the same permanent-marker gap, inherited
from #116, now closable with the same listing.

Full suite green under -race, golangci-lint clean. Verified each new guard fails
its test when removed.
